title: server-side sender approval still accepts non-ASCII/invisible/look-alike local parts: POST /calendar/join-rules/approvals -> recordApproval -> engine normalizeEmail only rejects whitespace, so a non-web client can store U+200B, U+202E or Cyrillic senders
evidence: Read of normalizeEmail: only checks one '@', non-empty local part without whitespace, ASCII domain. parseStrictEmail (captured senders) is printable-ASCII-only, so such stored approvals can never match a captured sender (inert, but they pollute the approvals list and render misleadingly). The web guard (ISS-T037UI-002 fix) is client-only.
fix_direction: Have the approval path (and rule-editor email matchers) use the printable-ASCII check of parseStrictEmail; 400 on others. Measure: U+200B, U+202E, U+0430 local parts each 400 via the API.

title: three copies of the printable-ASCII sender rule (apps/api sender-ascii.ts, apps/web editor, engine parseStrictEmail; plus core parseSender) with no cross-check test; they can drift
evidence: Only the class /^[!-~]+$/ is restated. Engine parseStrictEmail ALSO rejects length>320 and any of <>(),;:"\ and requires canonical form; the API gate does not (ASCII values like a<b@x.example pass the gate and are stored inert). Intentional per manifest, but nothing pins the two so a future engine change cannot silently diverge. dependency-cruiser forbids apps/* -> meeting-bot, so a direct import test is impossible.
fix_direction: Add one shared fixture list (JSON under contracts/ or qa/fixtures, accept/reject cases incl. U+200B, U+202E, U+0430, NBSP, BOM, punycode, <>(),;:"\ and 321-char) read via fs by a test in apps/api (gate) and a test in packages/meeting-bot (parseStrictEmail), each asserting its documented subset/superset relation.

title: sender-ascii tests only put the bad matcher in a single-rule set; mutation limiting ruleEmailMatchers to the first rule survives
fix_direction: Add a PUT case with a clean first rule and a non-ASCII email in rule 2/3.

title: fixture 'backslash' row is actually U+0008 (JSON "a " decodes to backspace); the backslash rejection is unpinned in both validators; no empty-string row
evidence: Node JSON.parse gives value length 12 with char 0x08. Mutants removing the backslash from the forbidden class survive: apps/api FORBIDDEN_SENDER_CHARS (api sender-ascii tests rc 0) and engine parseStrictEmail (sender-fixture.test rc 0). Fixture also has no "" row.
fix_direction: Change value to "a\b@x.example" (JSON-escaped backslash); add {"name":"empty","value":"","accept":false}; add a guard asserting every fixture value contains its named character (e.g. row 'backslash' includes \).
